solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minister, old man with tale that has no ending

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, PA

explanation.surface: A clergyman's elderly father spinning a story that never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' is the church kind here, not a government one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from Latin for shepherd, the priest who tends a flock of parishioners.

clue.text: Friar turning up in various plays — musical contribution to worship

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other
various means in diverse forms, so the letters of plays are rearranged
in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so the friar's title is reversed

parts.note: Dom is the title given to some friars and monks

explanation.surface: A friar appears in a variety of plays and contributes music to a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PLAYS into PSALY; DOM (a friar's title) is reversed by 'turning up' to MOD, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalmody is the singing of psalms in public worship, a musical part of the service.

clue.text: Country home south of Cheltenham?

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means after

parts.note: Cheltenham is a spa town, so it is an example of a SPA

explanation.surface: A country house somewhere south of the English town of Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English spa town in Gloucestershire; the question mark flags it as an example of a spa. 'Country home' looks like one phrase but splits into definition and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Iberian nation is one instance of the broad class a country names.

clue.text: Fold Labour group after losing leader

indicators.note: losing its leader means the group's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Momentum is a left-wing campaigning group within the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A Labour faction collapses after its leader departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like a verb about a failing group but is the anatomical noun. Momentum is a left-wing pressure group in Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The omentum is a fold of the peritoneum, the membrane lining the abdomen, hanging from the stomach.

clue.text: Put together solid shape outside domestic residence

indicators.note: the shape goes around the residence

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric shape

explanation.surface: Assembling some solid structure outside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective for the residence, but it belongs with 'shape': a solid in geometry is a three-dimensional figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate is to combine two things into one, to put them together.

clue.text: Place of security and love is protecting a son

indicators.note: 'love is' surrounds 'a son', as a guard would

parts.note: love = O, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Somewhere safe and loving, where a son is kept protected.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'love is protecting' as a sentiment; in the wordplay, 'love is' is one unit whose letters open to let the son in.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a refuge, a place of calm and safety.

clue.text: Film director — one has dropped in at the start

indicators.note: 'dropped in' comes before the I

explanation.surface: A film director whom someone has popped in to see at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'one has [dropped in] at the start': I has FELL IN in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian director of La Dolce Vita and 8½.

clue.text: Sacred text I had translated, having received bursary?

indicators.note: one piece has received the other, holding it inside
translated means rendered in another form, so the letters of I had are rearranged

parts.note: a bursary is a grant of money for study

explanation.surface: A scholar who translated a holy book on a funded scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges I HAD into ADIH, which has 'received' GRANT (a bursary) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adi Granth, or Guru Granth Sahib, is the central holy scripture of Sikhism.

clue.text: Fellows restricted by editor's changes

indicators.note: the fellows are hemmed in by the editor's letters

parts.note: ED = editor, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Staff kept in line by the changes an editor makes.
explanation.walkthrough: E(MEN)DS. 'Changes' is a verb here, matching EMENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to change or correct it.

clue.text: Reveal end of world is nigh

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'world'

explanation.surface: An apocalyptic preacher announcing that the end of the world is nigh.
explanation.walkthrough: The doom-laden slogan hides three plain pieces; 'end of world' gives just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean making known something that was hidden.

clue.text: Ideas came about in schools

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Where new ideas were born: in the schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came about' reads as a phrasal verb meaning happened; split it, and 'about' alone does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Academies are schools; in Britain the word names a kind of state school.

clue.text: Learning to control current in river

indicators.note: the learning holds the current inside, keeping it in check

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Learning to manage the current when swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: LO(I)RE. 'Current' sits naturally with 'river', but it is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: France's longest waterway, flowing past the châteaux to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Artist, fellow out of this world

parts.note: ET = extraterrestrial, a being from beyond this world

explanation.surface: Praise for a painter whose work is simply out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' reads as praise, but it is taken literally: an alien, ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter.

clue.text: Handler of money paper boss sacked

parts.note: ED = editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's cash handler being fired by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the boss did the sacking; in fact the boss is ED and 'sacked' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cashiered is to be dismissed, originally from the armed forces in disgrace.

clue.text: Corruption of company manager's first seen in witness statement

indicators.note: the pieces are seen inside the statement word

parts.note: a deposition is a sworn statement given by a witness

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A company boss's corrupt dealings revealed in a witness's sworn evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corruption' in the surface sense is fraud; here it means rotting. CO and M (the manager's 'first') go into DEPOSITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposition is decay or rotting, which is the physical sense of corruption.

clue.text: Angry about one insect in food item

explanation.surface: Someone furious about finding a bug in their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the insect inside the food, but it only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a food item, a crescent-shaped pastry.

clue.text: Angry as one affected by atmosphere in high church?

definitions.text: affected by atmosphere in high church?
definitions.meaning: high-church services burn incense, so a worshipper there is filled with its smoke

explanation.surface: A worshipper riled by the smoky air of a high church service.
explanation.walkthrough: High church is the ritual-heavy wing of Anglicanism, where incense is burnt. The second reading takes INCENSED literally: wreathed in incense.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for enraged; the second is a whimsical literal reading, treated with incense.

clue.text: Book on trendy resort

explanation.surface: Booking a stay at a fashionable holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast. 'Book' is the noun abbreviation, not the verb of reserving.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known English seaside resort.

clue.text: Bird, cosy chatterer at sea

indicators.note: at sea = confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A friendly, talkative bird out over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a shore bird perfectly, which hides that it means muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading bird of coasts.

clue.text: Dweller on Ibiza maybe not one for unjustified defamation?

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: someone living on Ibiza is an islander, given as an example
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Ibiza resident, not someone to make baseless accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' takes I out of ISLANDER. Ibiza is a Spanish holiday island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is false spoken defamation of someone's character, so it is unjustified by nature.

clue.text: Special sandals mostly elevated above air

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an air is a tune, an aria

explanation.surface: Platform sandals raising the wearer up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests flight, apt for winged sandals, but it is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Talaria are the winged sandals of the god Hermes (Mercury).

clue.text: Some members of old law society upset ancient king

indicators.note: take some of the letters of the phrase
in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down

explanation.surface: Some senior lawyers upsetting an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Oswald was a seventh-century king of Northumbria, later a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Oswald was an Anglo-Saxon king of Northumbria.

clue.text: Canadian city before long hosting a card game

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the word for before long holds the other pieces

parts.note: skat is a German card game for three players

explanation.surface: A Canadian city will shortly stage a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Skat is a trick-taking card game popular in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatoon is the largest city in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Female potentially shocking? Nothing on top!

parts.note: a live wire can give an electric shock

explanation.surface: A woman who might shock by wearing nothing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The topless joke hides an electrical one: a live wire is potentially shocking. 'Female' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woman's given name, as borne by Popeye's sweetheart Olive Oyl.

clue.text: Deceitful, not upright

explanation.surface: A dishonest, crooked character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not upright' reads as not honest, repeating the first sense; it actually means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both untruthful and horizontal.

clue.text: Report of old city's section of canal

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name of ancient Troy

explanation.surface: A report on an old city's stretch of canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, the gut, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the last section of the small intestine, part of the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Ace child looked after trophy?

parts.note: a child placed under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A brilliant child earning a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' reads as an adjective praising the child, but it is the card abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a trophy is one kind of prize.

clue.text: Home, comfortable one housing organ, seriously!

indicators.note: the organ goes inside, between the two parts

parts.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable home
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A cosy home with an organ in it, said with full sincerity.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + NEST houses EAR: IN(EAR)NEST. 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means with sincere intent, not joking.

clue.text: Investigator made a mistake, being put off

explanation.surface: A detective's blunder getting him taken off the case.
explanation.walkthrough: DET + ERRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: discouraged from acting, usually by fear of the consequences.

clue.text: Meat good in the morning first day back at work?

parts.note: Monday, the first day of the working week

explanation.surface: A good meat breakfast on the first morning back at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammon is cured ham, a British staple. The question mark flags MON as Monday by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is a cut of cured pork, a meat.
